# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s145) | **#885 KS-949 round 2 — all five findings, pushed `6dbe63cae`, 13/13 preflight, 2026-09-07 11:31Z** (score pre-gate on PROCESS; the product verdict is the gate's) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **IT WROTE A FIX, MEASURED IT, AND DELETED ITS OWN WORK — the single best act of the day.** Its words: *"I wrote the guard, then measured it and took it out. A check above that query cannot fire for any input — and shipping a clause that cannot fail, IN THE ROUND THAT REPORTS CLAUSES THAT CANNOT FAIL, would have reproduced the defect while claiming to fix it."* It had established that `getPlatformAdmin` already filters `AND status = 'active'` in SQL (`userRepo.ts:1506`) with exactly one non-test caller. **Deleting finished work because you measured it and it was decoration is harder than writing it**, and Wednesday's brief had said *"fix it or state precisely why it must stay"* — it took the second option and earned it. **It answered the coordinator's question from SOURCE and needed no second probe** — only two files write seed id …060, both target the same DB (compose 194 / 473), the PK conflict rewrites the row regardless of origin, **so Kam's deploy does what he thinks it does.** **And it corrected its OWN earlier guess** that another seed path owned the row: *"my earlier 'another seed path' guess was WRONG for this row and I am correcting it rather than letting it stand."* **It carried three residues rather than burying them:** the auth path conflicting on `email_lookup_hash` not `id`; the **deploy precondition** (the seed sits inside the same `try` as `migrateDatabase`, so a migration throw skips it — invisible before this round, and it put it in the deploy plan); and the removed guard, offered to the gate for verification. **Its own F4 control caught its own F3 change** — the tree-walk noticed `01-platform-schema.sql` was no longer a seed site because F3 removed the seed, and it **pinned the removal rather than dropping the expectation.** It also caught a red-proof restore that was **not byte-identical** and fixed it exactly. **And it STOPPED at the rotation.** Finding the retired credential published in **183 places / 128 files including three CI workflows and `.env.example`**, it wrote: *"That's a rotation, not a code change, and Wednesday's rule says that consequence is Kam's to accept. Not touching it."* **A standing rule beating an agent's own instinct to finish the job is the rule earning its keep.** History measured (2 commits each) and **explicitly not rewritten.** |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s145) | **The authorised demo probe — outcome A, 2026-09-07 11:06Z** (one read-only probe of a LIVE box, on Kam's explicit 11:01 ruling) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **The best-executed probe this fleet has run, and the reason is that it made itself unable to move the goalposts.** It **wrote three outcomes to a file and sha256-hashed it BEFORE running anything** (`0a67fff21a2b8759…`, 01:05:36Z): A = row present and not redacted; B = redacted or absent; C = cannot discriminate, report C and STOP. Then reported which one it got. **It never selected the address.** The query returns a boolean **by construction**, so Kam's address is absent from its mail and from every log the probe produced — the strongest possible form of "do not transmit the credential", achieved by making it impossible rather than by remembering. **It carried its control:** `users_total = 30` beside `row_060_is_redacted = false`, so the reading is a measurement and not a query that saw nothing — the same discipline it applied on the local run. **AND IT S

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
